CheckTitle: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore runtime with a JWT authorizer forwards the end-user token to the agent
CheckType: Software and Configuration Checks/AWS Security Best Practices/Runtime Behavior Analysis
Description: **Amazon Bedrock AgentCore runtimes** that authenticate callers with a **custom JWT authorizer** are evaluated for forwarding the `Authorization` header to the agent through `requestHeaderAllowlist`. Without it, the end-user token is validated at the runtime endpoint and then dropped, so the agent code never sees who the caller is.
Risk: When the token is dropped, every downstream tool call runs under the **agent execution role** instead of the originating user. This creates **confused-deputy** risk, where any authenticated user can reach data the role can reach, and removes **per-user authorization and audit trails** in downstream services.

Code.Other:
1. Open the Amazon Bedrock AgentCore console
2. Open Agent Runtimes and select the runtime
3. Under Request header configuration, add `Authorization` to the request header allowlist
4. Save the runtime configuration
5. In the agent code, pass the incoming token (or a token exchanged for it) to downstream tools

Recommendation.Text: Add `Authorization` to the **request header allowlist** of every AgentCore runtime that uses a **custom JWT authorizer**, and have the agent use that token, or a token exchanged for it, when calling downstream tools so each action is authorized as the originating user.

Notes: Runtimes that use IAM (SigV4) inbound authorization produce no finding, because their callers are IAM principals rather than end users. A runtime whose detail could not be retrieved also produces no finding. PASS confirms the token reaches the agent; whether the agent code passes it on to downstream tools cannot be verified from the control plane.
